newsitem.title: ISRAEL: French president to visit Knesset, ending row.
newsitem.headline: French president to visit Knesset, ending row.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac will visit Israel's parliament, defusing a diplomatic row with the Jewish state, Speaker Dan Tichon said on Sunday.

"The president of France will visit the Knesset on Tuesday -- how and when will be concluded today...I believe that in the end they understood in France that they made a mistake and they're right to fix this mistake," Tichon told Israel Television.

On Saturday, Tichon, a member of parliament from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party, said he would boycott Chirac's visit this week because it did not include a stop in the Knesset, Israel's parliament.
Chirac was due on Monday in Israel, the second destination in his six-day Middle East tour aimed at increasing European influence in peace moves in the region.
Tichon said while Chirac had cancelled his visit to the Knesset, he was planning to attend a session of the Palestinian National Council.
Tichon told the television that Israel's foreign ministry had called him early on Sunday to say the French ambassador would ensure Chirac visited the Knesset.

"I am happy to bring the good news that my demand was answered and he will come. It's not clear as yet whether he will speak or be satisfied with laying a wreath or a visit to the speaker's office," Tichon said.

"It's commonplace that presidents of the stature of the French president come for a visit at a time when the Knesset is in session and they visit the Knesset and a festive special session of the Knesset is convened."
Arab leaders have welcomed European involvement in the U.S.-mediated peace talks but Israel has been reluctant to give Europeans an official role.
Chirac arrived in Syria on Saturday at the start of his tour which also takes him to Jordan, Lebanon and Egypt.
